findings.evidence: Doc side — m149-projection-pushdown.md:54: "`SELECT *` (whole-row) -> `columns_needed` retorna `None` -> decode-tudo (fallback ADR-2). A/B byte-identico." Code side — columnar_project.rs:371-373 returns None ONLY when `att <= 0`; a `SELECT *`-expanded targetlist carries Vars with `varattno >= 1`, so line 378 `set.insert(idx)` runs for every column and line 381 returns `Some(...)`. The same conceptual conflation appears in the test comment columnar_project.rs:575 ("whole-row projection (`SELECT *`)") over a `SELECT a, b, c` query.
findings.message: Doc<->code drift: the benchmark doc states `SELECT *` (whole-row) makes columns_needed return None -> decode-all. Postgres expands `SELECT *` into per-column Vars (attno >= 1), so columns_needed returns Some(all-columns), never None. The A/B outcome (byte-identical) is correct, but the stated MECHANISM is wrong, and it masks the fact that the true None fallback (finding #1) is untested.
findings.remediation: Correct the doc (and the test comment at line 575) to distinguish `SELECT *` (columns_needed -> Some(all), materialize all) from a genuine whole-row Var / system column `SELECT ctid` (columns_needed -> None, decode-all fallback). Only the latter exercises the None path.

findings.evidence: Two seams do the same header-read + directory-deserialize + per-wanted-column `read_chunked -> zstd::decode_all -> codec::decode_column`: `decode_columns` loop at columnar.rs:842-850 (keyed by `wanted: &[usize]`) and `decode_stripe` loop at columnar.rs:726-738 (keyed by `want_mask: &[bool]`). Plan ADR-3 (.claude/knowledge-base/plans/m149-projection-pushdown-plan.md:63-66) DECIDED: 'Reusar `decode_columns` + `deform_rows_into_columns` (nao duplicar o seam de leitura)' and rejected 'um decode-por-projecao novo -- duplicaria conhecimento'. findings.message: M149 added a SECOND column-projection stripe-decode seam (`decode_stripe`/`form_row` threading `want_mask: &[bool]`) instead of consuming the pre-existing `decode_columns(projection: Option<&[usize]>)` seam that the plan's ADR-3 prescribed. The 'skip read_chunked+zstd on unprojected columns' knowledge now lives in two paths with two encodings, exactly the alternative ADR-3 rejected as DRY-breaking.
findings.remediation: Extract a single `decode_chunk_group(entries, cg, natts, cols, want) -> Vec<Vec<Option<Vec<u8>>>>` consumed by BOTH decode_columns and decode_stripe; keep only the thin column-major vs row-major (`form_row`) output adapters distinct — honoring ADR-3's single-read-seam decision.

findings.evidence: decode_stripe:727-729 `if !want_mask[col] { cgcols.push(Vec::new()); continue; }` skips the per-chunk read_chunked/zstd (l.732-737); load_next_batch builds want_mask from scan_projection (columnar.rs:1066-1078); comment l.694-696 documents the decode-skip.
findings.message: Performance/memory — addressed: masked-out columns skip read_chunked + zstd decode and are never allocated (placeholder Vec::new()), so projected scans materialize O(wanted) column buffers per stripe instead of all 105, and peak memory stays O(one stripe) via the lazy load_next_batch.

findings.evidence: load_next_batch@1066-1078 rebuilds `let mut m = vec![false; natts]; for &c in w.iter() { if c < natts { m[c]=true } }` — converting the index list to a bool mask; decode_columns@784 keeps the index-list form.
findings.message: Two column-selection representations coexist in columnar.rs: the scan path uses a per-column `want_mask: &[bool]` (decode_stripe/form_row, absolute-index NULL writing) while the DataFusion path uses `projection: Option<&[usize]>` -> positional `wanted` (decode_columns). load_next_batch bridges scan_projection's `Rc<Vec<usize>>` into a fresh `Vec<bool>` on every stripe. A future third columnar consumer must pick between the two; the divergence is DOCUMENTED and justified (form_row needs absolute indices; decode_columns returns positional), so this is an advisory extensibility note, not a defect.

findings.evidence: columnar.rs:1067 `match crate::am::columnar_project::scan_projection(st as usize)` — storage AM reaching into the query-planning module. findings.message: Coupling-direction note (not a fixable defect): the low-level storage TableAM `columnar.rs` compile-time depends UP on the planner-integration module `columnar_project::scan_projection`, and the cross-module contract is an untyped `usize` raw-address key. This is essential (the PG18 TableAM `scan_begin` carries no column bitmap — ADR-1) and mirrors the accepted vecfilter precedent; recorded for boundary visibility, not remediation.

Verified as a STUDIED STANDARD, not a port: columns_needed() implements the canonical PG technique (pull_var_clause(targetlist)∪pull_var_clause(qual) → BTreeSet<usize> of 0-based attnos) in idiomatic Rust (Option/Rc/RefCell/thread_local); Citus ColumnarAttrNeeded is C returning a Bitmapset with distinct identifiers (neededColumns/attr_needed) — convergent, not copied. findings.evidence: Line 28: `#![allow(non_snake_case)]`. Verified reproducibly: `grep -nE '(let|fn) +[a-z]+[A-Z]' theodb_rs/src/am/columnar_project.rs` returns NONE FOUND. Contrast lib.rs:21 where `#[allow(non_snake_case)]` is legitimately needed for the required C symbol `_PG_init`. An unused allow is not compiler-warned, so it is silent cruft rather than a defect.

findings.remediation: Drop the module-level `#![allow(non_snake_case)]` (no non-snake identifiers exist here); keep allows narrowly scoped to the item that needs them, as lib.rs does for `_PG_init`.

findings.evidence: columnar_project.rs mirrors customscan.rs symbol-for-symbol: swap_active (project:62 / custom:62), ActiveGuard+Drop (project:80,86 / custom:106,112), node registry NODE_PROJECTIONS/NODE_MEMBERSHIPS + registry_insert/get/remove (project:58,92,97,100 / custom:50,78,86,90), clear_all/clear_all_memberships (project:108 / custom:98), `static mut PREV_HOOK` (project:148 / custom:219), RegisterXactCallback+RegisterSubXactCallback (project:174-175 / custom:266-267). The only real variation is the registry/slot KEY (scandesc-matched tuple vs bare Option).
findings.message: The CustomScan side-channel correctness protocol — thread_local ACTIVE slot + swap_active + RAII ActiveGuard(Drop) + node-keyed registry (insert/get/remove) + clear_all + Xact/SubXact abort-clear callbacks — is duplicated near-verbatim from customscan.rs (the vecfilter). Two independently-maintained copies of a subtle install/restore-on-longjmp/clear-on-abort protocol will drift.
findings.remediation: Extract a generic `am/customscan_support.rs` with `ActiveSlot<K,V>` + `NodeRegistry<V>` + `ActiveGuard<K,V>` + a shared xact/subxact clear helper; parameterize the key type so vecfilter (unit key) and projection (scandesc key) reuse one audited protocol.

findings.evidence: Line 63: `SCAN_PROJECTION.with(|c| std::mem::replace(&mut *c.borrow_mut(), v))`. `RefCell::<T>::replace(&self, t) -> T` is defined in std as exactly `mem::replace(&mut *self.borrow_mut(), t)` — the manual form re-derives a stdlib method, carrying an extra explicit borrow and a `std::mem::` path for no behavioral gain.
findings.message: swap_active hand-rolls RefCell::replace via mem::replace(&mut *borrow_mut(), v); the std method exists.
findings.remediation: Use the RefCell idiom: `SCAN_PROJECTION.with(|c| c.replace(v))` (identical semantics, no manual borrow).

findings.evidence: nested-scan: test_nested_self_join_projection adicionado; self-join A/B byte-identico provado no droplet. commit ab8a5f4
findings.message: Nested-scan projection correctness — the SINGLE reason the side channel is keyed by the scan descriptor — has zero regression test. No test drives a subplan that scans a DIFFERENT theodb_columnar table during qual evaluation while an outer projection scan is active, i.e. the exact scenario the scandesc key exists to prevent from silently projecting the wrong columns.
findings.remediation: Add an A/B pg_test with two columnar tables where the outer projection scan's WHERE contains a correlated subquery scanning the second columnar table (e.g. `SELECT a FROM t_col x WHERE b <> (SELECT max(b) FROM t_col2 y WHERE y.a = x.a)`), asserting columnar == heap twin — a RED that fails if the scandesc match is removed.

findings.evidence: struct ActiveGuard(Option<(usize, Rc<Vec<usize>>)>); impl Drop for ActiveGuard { fn drop(&mut self){ let _ = swap_active(self.0.take()); } } (lines 80-90); installed at exec_custom_scan:460
findings.message: RAII / Scoped-Guard — applied_correctly: ActiveGuard::install(v) swaps the thread-local ACTIVE side-channel slot and its Drop restores the previous value, so a PG ERROR→Rust unwind at the #[pg_guard] boundary mid-ExecScan can never leave a stale projection installed. Correct save/restore (re-entrant), belt-and-braces with the xact/subxact clears.

findings.evidence: NODE_PROJECTIONS is a thread_local HashMap (l.58) removed at end_custom_scan:468 and wiped by clear_all() (l.108-111) registered on Xact/SubXact abort (l.174-175, 182-204); ActiveGuard::drop restores the prior slot (l.86-90). Registry is bounded by the count of live projection nodes in the current plan.
findings.message: Fault tolerance — addressed: transient projection state is bounded to one (sub)transaction — the Rc<Vec> registry lives Rust-side (not in the palloc0'd ProjScanState so PG frees never skip Drop), the pull-window swap is an RAII ActiveGuard restored even on longjmp, and xact/subxact abort clears orphaned entries + the active slot, closing the scandesc ABA window.

findings.evidence: Identical two-line wrapper at columnar_project.rs:114-115, customscan.rs:188-189, and columnar_agg.rs:25-26 (rule-of-3 crossed).
findings.message: `struct Methods<T>(T); unsafe impl<T> Sync for Methods<T> {}` — the blanket-Sync wrapper for CustomScan method tables — is copy-pasted into a third CustomScan module. A hand-rolled `unsafe impl Sync` replicated three times is a soundness surface that should be declared once.
findings.remediation: Move `Methods<T>` + its `unsafe impl Sync` into one shared module (e.g. am/customscan_support.rs) and `use` it from the three providers.

findings.evidence: static PATH_METHODS/SCAN_METHODS/EXEC_METHODS: Methods(pg_sys::Custom*Methods{...}) at lines 117,123,128; pg_sys::RegisterCustomScanMethods(&SCAN_METHODS.0) at line 171
findings.message: CustomScan Provider — applied_correctly: PG18 provider protocol implemented as three function-pointer vtables (CustomPathMethods@117, CustomScanMethods@123, CustomExecMethods@128) registered once via RegisterCustomScanMethods@171; the node IS the scan (scanrelid=rel.relid, no children) — the canonical way to see plan->targetlist/qual that a pure TableAM cannot (module doc §Why). Mirrors the prior art (customscan.rs) and Citus ColumnarAttrNeeded (GoF Strategy via C vtable; Fowler/PG provider contract).

findings.evidence: subxact_clear/registry: mesmo fix do ABA (registry_remove no None). regression subxact-abort provado no droplet. commit ab8a5f4
findings.message: subxact_clear clears only the ACTIVE slot (swap_active(None)) on SUBXACT_EVENT_ABORT_SUB but never prunes NODE_PROJECTIONS; the registry is cleared only by clear_all() at OUTER xact end. After a caught PL/pgSQL EXCEPTION that longjmps out of a projection scan before end_custom_scan runs, its {node_ptr -> wanted} entry is orphaned for the rest of the transaction. A later ProjScanState palloc'd at the same address (ABA) whose begin takes the columns_needed==None fallback (whole-row/system-column, e.g. SELECT ctid FROM t_col) does NOT registry_insert, so exec_custom_scan's registry_get(node) at line 459 reads the STALE wanted set and installs it as the active projection -> columnar decodes only the stale columns and NULLs the rest -> silent wrong answer. The module's own clear_all note (lines 105-107) says clearing 'closes the ABA window where a new scandesc ... could inherit a stale projection', but that guarantee holds only at xact end, not across a subxact abort.
findings.remediation: In subxact_clear, prune the registry for the aborting subxact (or call clear_all() as xact_clear does) so no orphaned NODE_PROJECTIONS entry survives; OR make exec trust only state established by its own begin (per-node generation token) instead of a bare pointer-keyed lookup.

findings.evidence: lizard: 'pathlist_hook@212-287 ... 20 CCN, 67 NLOC' (measured McCabe CC=20 > 15).
findings.message: pathlist_hook has measured cyclomatic complexity 20 (McCabe), above the lizard default threshold of 15 — the flagship M149 planner hook concentrates AM-detection guards, aggregate-query exclusion, and the cheapest-seqscan search in one body.
findings.remediation: Extract the cheapest-unparameterized-seqscan search (lines 252-266) into a `cheapest_seqscan(rel)` helper and the eligibility guards (reloptkind/RTE/amoid/aggregate checks, lines 224-247) into `is_projection_eligible(root, rel, rte)` — each returns Option, dropping the hook body below CC 15.

findings.evidence: pathlist_hook calls `prev(root, rel, _rti, rte)` first (columnar_project.rs:218-220); PREV_HOOK is captured in init() AFTER customscan::init (l.172, lib.rs:29→37 init order); the aggregate guard returns early (l.239-247). Confirmed 0 result divergence + 38/38 agg queries unchanged in docs/benchmarks/m149-projection-pushdown.md:13-15,55-56.
findings.message: Integration/data-flow — addressed: the projection pathlist hook composes without editing customscan.rs (saves PREV_HOOK and calls the vecfilter hook first) and declines aggregate queries (hasAggs/groupClause/groupingSets/hasWindowFuncs) so columnar_agg's find_scan_relid (which matches T_SeqScan, not this CustomScan) and the vectorized-agg path stay intact.

findings.evidence: columnar_project.rs line 268: `let total = (*seq).total_cost * 0.9;` — the 0.9 factor is a constant, not a function of |wanted|/natts; columns_needed (lines 350-382) returns Some(all) for SELECT * (explicit column Vars), so want_mask is all-true and decode_stripe skips no column, but add_path still installs the cheaper CustomPath.
findings.message: The projection CustomPath is priced at 0.9x the seqscan total_cost UNCONDITIONALLY (`let total = (*seq).total_cost * 0.9;`), independent of how many columns are actually projected. For a whole-row / SELECT * query columns_needed returns Some(all-columns) so the node decodes every column (want_mask all-true == pre-M149 work) yet still wins the plan by 10% while adding the side-channel install + registry churn per pull — a net-negative plan for the zero-benefit case. Contract smell: the cost claims a saving the node does not deliver when nothing is projected away.
findings.remediation: Scale the discount by the projected fraction (e.g. only discount when |wanted| < natts, or price ~ startup + total*(0.1 + 0.9*|wanted|/natts)) so a whole-row projection does not win the plan for no benefit.

findings.message: O path e priced 0.9x o seq com disabled_nodes=0 (alloc_node zera). Sob enable_seqscan=off (PG17+ marca disabled_nodes=1), o nosso path fica 0 e domina o seq que o usuario desabilitou. Resultado correto, so surpresa de planner-preference.
findings.remediation: path.disabled_nodes = (*seq).disabled_nodes

findings.evidence: columnar_project.rs:271-286 builds the CustomPath but sets no path.parallel_safe / parallel_workers, adds no partial path, and EXEC_METHODS leaves EstimateDSMCustomScan/InitializeDSMCustomScan/InitializeWorkerCustomScan = None (l.137-139). The thread_local SCAN_PROJECTION side-channel (l.51-54) cannot cross into parallel-worker processes by construction. Sibling columnar_agg.rs:847 DOES propagate parallel_safe; this node does not. The benchmark regime is serial (tests set max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 0, columnar_project.rs:496); docs/benchmarks/m149-projection-pushdown.md does not disclose the parallel setting for the 300k/500k-row hits runs on the 8-vCPU box.
findings.message: Scalability — missing_required: the projection CustomPath is serial-only, so at ClickBench/columnar scale the planner picks a parallel seqscan and projection pushdown silently does not engage (fail-safe but the 3.73x win vanishes exactly in the large-analytic regime the columnar store targets).
findings.remediation: Either make projection parallel-aware (mark the path parallel_safe, generate a partial CustomPath + DSM callbacks, and install `wanted` per worker instead of via a thread_local), OR document in the benchmark + plan that projection is serial-only and disclose the parallel GUC used, so the 3.73x is not read as a production-scale claim.

findings.evidence: ABA stale-registry: begin sincroniza o registry em ambos os ramos (None=>registry_remove). Provado no droplet (build cassert): test regression subxact-abort passa (pos-abort o fallback nao herda mask stale). commit ab8a5f4
findings.message: begin_custom_scan insere no NODE_PROJECTIONS so no ramo Some; o ramo None (fallback) nao insere nem remove. subxact_clear limpa so o ACTIVE slot, nao o registry (clear_all so em top-xact). Trigger: Q1 (Some) sofre EXCEPTION num subxact PL/pgSQL -> end_custom_scan pulado -> entrada {addr->wanted} orfa; Q2 (None, ex SELECT ctid) reusando o addr NAO remove -> exec le a projecao stale -> decodifica so colunas stale -> resultado NULL errado silencioso. 3 analises convergiram (council rust-pgrx, council index-storage, pilar code). O irmao customscan.rs e imune (insert incondicional + flag membership_active). Remediacao unanime: None => registry_remove(node).

findings.evidence: grep for log!/warning!/notice!/pgstat/counter/metric/histogram in columnar_project.rs returns 0 matches. exec_custom_scan:458-459 chooses install-vs-fallback (`registry_get(node).map(...)`) with no observable signal; the only surface is the EXPLAIN node text asserted in tests (l.525).
findings.message: Observability — missing_required: the projection path degrades silently to decode-all in two runtime cases (columns_needed==None fallback, and non-projection scans) with no counter/log to see it; a plan change that stops engaging the node is invisible except by manually re-running EXPLAIN.
findings.remediation: Emit a lightweight runtime signal on the fallback branch (e.g. a DEBUG1 log or a pg_stat counter of projected-vs-decode-all scans) so silent non-engagement after a plan change is detectable in production without re-EXPLAINing.

findings.evidence: `sed -n '486,607p' columnar_project.rs | grep -Ei 'rescan|enable_projection = off|EXCEPTION'` returns NO MATCH — the 4 tests never run a nested-loop join (which alone triggers `rescan_custom_scan` at line 479 via `pg_sys::table_rescan`), never set `enable_projection = off` (seed() sets it ON at line 494 only), and never open/abort a subtransaction. rescan is invoked from a real plan shape (NL inner), unlike the pure defense-in-depth subxact/GUC guards.
findings.message: Three functional/defensive paths carry no test: rescan_custom_scan (nested-loop inner re-execution, line 479), the `theodb.enable_projection = off` fallback to the plain seqscan (line 221), and the subxact-abort active-slot clear after a caught PL/pgSQL EXCEPTION (line 199-204). The first is a real result-bearing path (a nested-loop join re-scanning the columnar inner) that would produce wrong rows if broken.
findings.remediation: Add at least (a) an A/B nested-loop join test (`SET enable_hashjoin=off; enable_mergejoin=off`) forcing the columnar projection scan as the NL inner and asserting columnar == heap, exercising rescan; and (b) a test with `SET theodb.enable_projection = off` asserting the plan is a plain Seq Scan and the result still equals the heap twin.

findings.evidence: fallback None: test_fallback_system_column adicionado (ctid -> None real); system-col A/B byte-identico provado no droplet. commit ab8a5f4
findings.message: The `columns_needed` decode-all fallback (the `att <= 0` None branch: whole-row Var + system column) — described in-code as the ADR-2 'correctness floor' — is NOT exercised by any test. `test_fallback_whole_row` runs `SELECT a, b, c` (all attno >= 1), which registers wanted={0,1,2} and never returns None; the plan's promised `SELECT ctid` / whole-row A/B test was silently dropped.
findings.remediation: Add an A/B pg_test that actually reaches the None branch: `SELECT ctid FROM t_col ORDER BY a` (system column) and a whole-row `SELECT t_col FROM t_col ORDER BY a`, each asserting the columnar result equals the heap twin — proving decode-all fires and stays byte-identical when columns_needed returns None.
